note.backdrop: A third session of the tech sell-off, now pulling the whole market: before the open the S&P 500 is -1.9%, the Nasdaq 100 -2.9%, small caps -1.3%, and the VIX +16.9%, so rising fear and a market-wide move were both flagged. Chips lead again (semiconductors' median -4.5%; AMD -5.9%, 8.4% below Friday's close; Micron -6.8%, Nvidia -5.6% at 8:01 a.m. ET), and StockTitan counts about 74% of Monday's Nasdaq 100 gain gone. Last night's reports are met by sharp falls (Ambarella, Nutanix, Urban Outfitters, Dell, Workday). The 8:30 a.m. ET data (GDP, personal income and spending with PCE inflation, durable goods, jobless claims) came out as this check read the market and is not in it.

themes.beneath: Monday's +7.00% Nasdaq 100 day rested on one board decision (Nvidia's CEO); two sessions later about three quarters of it is gone (StockTitan), and AMD is now below its Friday close. Tuesday's rotation into retail and drug makers does not hold this morning: the move is broad, not a rotation (inferred from the market line).
themes.cause: AI and chip stocks fall for a third session as the sell-off gathers pace before Thanksgiving (Yahoo, StockTitan); the Dow is lower too and Anthropic trades further below its offering price. The VIX rose 16.9% before the open.
themes.mechanism: The same high-beta AI names lead (in the check: semiconductors' median -4.5%), and this morning the broad market follows: SPY -1.9% against QQQ -2.9%. Veeco, a chip-equipment maker, -11.3% with the market carrying -5.1% at its beta of 2.67.

themes.beneath: What the price expected (the case file's [e:] lines): Ambarella and Nutanix had both sold off into their reports (-1.3 and -1.7 of their usual months) and fell again: capitulation, in the library's names. X1a's tilt says a stock that sold off falls a little less often on its report day; these fell anyway, which is what a tilt of a point or two allows. Dell recovered part of its fall (-5.2% at 8:01 a.m. from -6.9% earlier, StockTitan).
themes.cause: Ambarella's revenue forecast ($70-75 million against $115.2 million), with Morgan Stanley downgrading it (s6); Nutanix's revenue +15% with its CEO to step down once a successor takes over; Urban Outfitters' record sales but Anthropologie weakness and a cautious holiday outlook, with Morgan Stanley downgrading it to Equal Weight (s2, s18); Dell's record revenue and $132.3 billion AI backlog; Workday's slower fourth quarter.
themes.mechanism: Each falls on its own report (Ambarella -30.1% of its own, Nutanix -10.2%, Urban Outfitters -10.6%), on a morning the market carries -2% more. Ambarella's partners fell about as much as the chip group (Ceva -4.0%, Rambus -5.2%, Alpha and Omega -5.7% against the median -4.5%): the pond puts the rest on the group, not on Ambarella.
